assessments.reasoning: The retained original of Borland’s Delphi 7 guide, preserved through a third-party copy, identifies Pascal as the base language and attributes object-oriented additions to Delphi. That relationship supports the index’s dialect classification for the language documented in this edition. The classification is the index’s inference.

challenge.method: Does the chapter merely compare Delphi objects with a Pascal feature, or does it identify a language-level relationship?
challenge.results: The opening description establishes the relationship independently of the later analogy with records. It identifies no ISO edition and makes no conformance finding.

limitations: The guide uses standard Pascal as the base language without citing an ISO revision here. This classification does not assert complete ISO/IEC 7185 conformance.
The evidence applies to the Borland Delphi 7 language variety. Other Object Pascal traditions and later Delphi releases require separate evidence.
